item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"high","summary":"B is closer to the frozen contract because it preserves FilesService.Add and limits the production change to the new Upload API. It still needs revision to delegate to Add and improve tests, but A introduces a broader, explicitly disallowed behavioral change to Add.","reasons":["A changes Add to eagerly read and buffer every caller-supplied body. That alters the lower-level API's streaming, memory, timing, and reader-error behavior despite the contract requiring Add's behavior to remain unchanged.","A's Upload calls a new private add helper instead of routing through the existing public Add method, while also adding documentation that advertises the out-of-scope Add behavior change.","B correctly uses multipartbody.NewFile with field \"file\", validates empty filename and nil content before encoding, and preserves Add unchanged.","B duplicates Add's option handling, request execution, response decoding, and error handling instead of calling s.Add(ctx, body, contentType, opts...), violating the required reuse pattern and creating maintenance drift, but this is a localized defect compared with A's API behavior change."],"risks_a":["Eager io.ReadAll in Add can cause unexpectedly large memory use or hang on long-lived readers that previously streamed during the request.","Add now consumes the source before request construction and wraps source errors differently, changing observable behavior.","Neither validation nor source-reader error tests are added, and Upload bypasses Add."],"risks_b":["Upload duplicates Add internals, so future changes to options, decoding, or errors may diverge.","The multipart test checks the field and filename but never verifies uploaded content.","The retry test exercises a generic bytes.Reader rather than Upload with streamed content, and validation/source-reader error cases are untested."]}
